summary.headline: Midwest Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY and PAT 27%, with granite carrying results and quartz Phase 1 still ramping (~5,000 t sold, ~INR5 crore revenue).
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 35% YoY, EBITDA up 25% and PAT up 27%, with most of the earnings from granite despite diesel cost pressure. Quartz Phase 1 has begun commercial operations with roughly INR5 crore revenue and about 5,000 tonnes sold in the quarter, and management is targeting a 10,000 t/month run rate by end-Q2 and 15,000 t/month by Q4. FY27 guidance is about INR840 crore revenue (granite INR720 crore, quartz INR100-120 crore), with quartz EBITDA expected to be low this year. Management also flagged an Indonesia MoU with PERMINAS for rare earth oxides and an imminent Sri Lanka licence step, while Kerala remains stalled on government transition.

financial_highlights.value: ~10% in both Absolute Black and Black Galaxy

financial_highlights.metric: Blended EBITDA margin impact from diesel (Q1 FY27)
financial_highlights.change: Diesel ~13% of cost; diesel rose from ~INR85 to INR125-130/litre

segments.name: Granite (natural stone)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth above 30% excluding quartz; volumes up ~10% in both Absolute Black and Black Galaxy, with better realisations and a price hike of about 3-5%. Electrified fleet and solar backing cut diesel sensitivity.

segments.name: Quartz (engineered stone, Phase 1, Kerala-linked plant)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR5 crore on ~5,000 t sold; realisation about INR10,000/t. Mix about 65% engineered stone and 35% solar. Break-even targeted around 10,000 t/month, with plant capacity up to 18,000 t/month.

segments.name: Rare earth / Midwest Advanced Materials
segments.commentary: Sister concern Midwest Advanced Materials focuses on rare earth oxide to permanent magnet. Parent scope is ore-to-oxide via a JV with PERMINAS; no revenue yet, with cash flows expected FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue estimated at ~INR840 crore vs INR645 crore in FY26; management called this conservative and said Q1 run-rate suggests beating it.
Quartz: ~120,000 t production target for FY27 (revised down from 150,000 t); quartz EBITDA this year to be below expectations; break-even around 10,000 t/month, with some profit expected by year-end.
Granite EBITDA margin in line with prior years, with 50-100 bps diesel-related variance; blended EBITDA margin expected in the 26-27% range for FY27.

FY28: quartz Phase 1 revenue INR180-200 crore plus Phase 2 contribution of about INR40-50 crore (around 4 months of production); granite growth 10-12%; blended EBITDA ~29-30%, with quartz EBITDA slightly above 30%.
Sri Lanka: policy finalised; land/licence documentation expected this quarter, groundbreaking around October, 12-15 months build-out; cash flows now expected FY29.
Indonesia (PERMINAS): MoU to be converted to an agreement this quarter and a JV formed next quarter; project report due in 45-60 days; capex to be given next call.
capex_capacity: Quartz Phase 2: total capex ~INR125 crore, with ~INR60-70 crore in Q2-Q3 and the balance in Q4 or early FY28; commissioning now 10-12 months out after machinery was resourced away from China; funded by fresh equity raised.
Quartz Phase 1 capacity can reach 18,000 t/month; 15,000 t/month is the planned stable run rate; ramp to 10,000-12,000 t/month in Q2 and above 15,000 t/month by Q4.
Sri Lanka plant capex ~INR120 crore (internal accruals); Kerala (KMML) pilot plant described as low cost, with no activity pending new government and MD appointment.
Indonesia capex to be higher than Kerala given overseas mining; figure to be given next call.
Electrification of the granite fleet mostly completed this year; regular granite replacement capex funded from operating cash flow.
demand_pricing: Quartz volumes are mostly exported to China; management said Q4 typically carries 30-40% of annual revenue due to Chinese New Year restocking.
Granite pricing improved; a further price increase of about 3-5% was taken to offset fuel costs. Management said no further price action is planned this year unless fuel moves again.
Fuel prices eased slightly from Q1 peaks but remain well above prior-year levels; management expects margin recovery in Q2.
Q3 monsoon risk noted: production is typically lower in Q3 due to rains.
Freight is generally on FOB terms, so freight costs are borne by customers and are not in Midwest's cost base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 quartz volume and the ramp-up timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5,000 t sold in Q1; management guided ~20,000 t this quarter (likely a typo for run rate), 10,000-12,000 t next quarter and above 15,000 t in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will quartz reach EBITDA break-even and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even expected around Q3 FY27 at about 10,000 t/month, with some profit by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 150,000 t FY27 quartz production target still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management revised the target to about 120,000 t after a technical production issue that has since been resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue look lower than Q4 and how does the quartz capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is seasonally the peak (30-40% of annual revenue) due to Chinese New Year restocking; Phase 2 capex is INR125 crore spread over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 see higher margins with quartz?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Blended EBITDA expected at 29-30% in FY28, with quartz EBITDA slightly above 30%, given Phase 1 revenue of INR180-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Which granite mine has the AP government revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Black Galaxy; the arrangement is a revenue-share payment to a state-owned lessor that also holds equity.

risks_watch: Quartz Phase 1 ramp: management targets 10,000-12,000 t/month in Q2 and above 15,000 t/month by Q4 versus ~5,000 t sold in Q1; any slip delays break-even (guided around Q3 FY27).
Quartz FY27 production target cut from 150,000 t to ~120,000 t after a technical issue; management says it is now resolved, but this is a credibility point to verify next quarter.

Diesel exposure: diesel ~13% of costs and prices moved from ~INR85 to INR125-130/litre; Q1 blended EBITDA margin fell 190 bps. Management expects Q2 recovery and relies on price hikes of about 3-5% and electrification.
Q3 monsoon: production typically lower in Q3; management says it is better prepared than in Q1.
Phase 2 quartz capex of ~INR125 crore funded by fresh equity; commissioning now 10-12 months out after machinery was re-sourced away from China. Watch the Q2-Q3 spend of INR60-70 crore.

Overseas projects still early: Indonesia (PERMINAS) capex, equity split and project report not yet available (due in 45-60 days); Sri Lanka licence documentation and October groundbreaking; Kerala (KMML) stalled pending a new MD and government team. Cash flows from Sri Lanka and Indonesia now pencilled in for FY29.
key_quotes: And we are in line to reach the target for the year end.
So we will be converting the MOU to a agreement or this quarter itself most likely and next quarter we will be forming a JV.
We are not doing 150,000 tons, we will be doing around 120,000, so that is the effect of that.
So war, no war, we will not be affected on the granite margins going forward.
Yes, we have start the commercial operations, the teething issues are behind us.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's growth, the granite franchise and the Sri Lanka and Indonesia timelines, but noticeably hedged on specifics: many answers defer capex, returns and timing to the next call, and Kerala is described as stalled. Management was cautious on quartz volumes and FY27 revenue, calling its INR840 crore guidance conservative.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at ~INR840 cr vs INR645 cr in FY26 (~31% growth), backed by granite volume growth (~10%) and price hikes of 3-5%, plus quartz Phase 1 ramp (~INR5 cr in Q1, targeting 10,000 t/month by end-Q2); quartz FY27 volume cut to 120,000 t from 150,000 t and Phase 2 commissioning is 10-12 months away, so backing is partial.
